content: The Vice Chancellor (VC) of Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University (SBBWU), Peshawar is Prof. Dr. Safia Ahmad who is  the chief executive and academic head of the university.
The Vice Chancellor is the main executive and academic head. They ensure all university laws, rules, and regulations are properly followed.
The Pro-Vice Chancellor acts as Vice Chancellor when the regular VC is on leave, abroad, or the position is vacant.
The Registrar is a full-time officer and custodian of the university seal. They handle general administration, academic matters, and staff establishment.
The Treasurer manages financial operations, prepares the annual budget, and releases funds according to approved allocations.
The Controller of Examinations manages all university examinations from undergraduate to PhD level.
The Media and Protocol Section handles university publicity through print and electronic media and highlights academic, co-curricular, and research activities.
The Quality Enhancement Cell (QEC) is headed by the Dean and focuses on continuous improvement, capacity building, and preparing students and staff for future challenges.
The Planning and Development Directorate supports university growth by introducing new disciplines and managing development projects.
The Provost Office is responsible for managing hostel administration for students.
Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University Peshawar is the first public sector women university in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The university was named to honor Benazir Bhutto and other women of Pakistan who contributed to women empowerment and national development.
The campus was inaugurated on 1 September 2004 by the Chief Minister of KPK.
The university was established under the Frontier Women University Act 2004, later published in 2005 as a provincial act.
The first Vice Chancellor, Prof. Dr. Syeda Farhana Jahangir, was appointed on 10 June 2005.
The university initially operated from the Department of Psychology at the University of Peshawar and became functional in a college hostel building.
In February 2006, academic activities started with 8 departments including Arabic, Psychology, Computer Science, Islamiat, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, and English with 240 students.
In 2007, land of 400 kanals was allotted but initially occupied, and a PC-I project worth 456 million rupees was approved.
New disciplines like Bioinformatics and Microbiology were introduced in 2007 along with a Clinical Psychology diploma and psychotherapeutic clinic.
Women Development Center and Education Department were established in 2008, introducing B.Ed, diplomas, and certificate programs.
MPhil and PhD programs started in English, Islamiat, and Psychology. Several colleges were affiliated and international MoUs were signed with UK universities.
In 2010, new disciplines like Law, Political Science, Urdu, Management Sciences, and Art & Design were introduced.
The university was renamed from Frontier Women University to Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University through a legal amendment in 2010.
In 2012, MS programs and MPhil leading to PhD in Economics, Computer Science, and Management Sciences were introduced under the KPK Universities Act 2012.
By 2012, the university had 4600 students in 18 departments and 16 affiliated colleges with over 5000 students.
The university built academic blocks, hostels, administration block, and IT infrastructure including a high-speed network and wireless system.
The university was ranked 9th by HEC among 27 new universities in Pakistan despite security and infrastructure challenges.
Education is essential for national development and economic growth. Increasing literacy rate is key for reducing poverty.
Pakistan invests in education to improve human resources and economic productivity through skill development.
The university aims to provide quality education to women across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including remote areas.
The institution focuses on academic, moral, physical, professional, and spiritual development of students.
The university has expanded disciplines continuously since 2005 and remains the largest provider of female education in KPK.
Modern facilities include IT centers, research units, accommodation near campus, and industry-linked programs for employability.
